members.statement: In the stated marked-incidence deformation problem with smooth leading plane cubic, every positive first-normal jet lies in the gauge image; the Hesse and Fermat model calculations give the exact determinant and rank certificates used by the global bundle argument.
members.title: Smooth Leading Cubics Have No Positive First-Normal Moduli

members.statement: For the analyzed minimal smooth defect end, the local sign-three torsor group is K_loc congruent to C[3] congruent to F_3^2, and its two nonzero directions are represented by algebraic finite covers over the henselian local end.
members.title: The Minimal Smooth Defect End Has Two Algebraic Sign-Three Torsors

members.statement: Show that at least one nonzero class in the local F_3^2 sign-torsor space globalizes across the boundary; this would contradict the absence of nontrivial finite etale covers of affine three-space.
members.title: Does a Local Sign-Three Torsor Survive the Global Keller Boundary?

members.statement: For the quadratic resolvent Q of a complex cubic Keller normalization, an isolated singularity cannot support a nonflat cubic defect; moreover, three-torsion in Cl(Q) is detected at the height-two singular primes.
members.title: A Cubic Defect Forces a Nonisolated Quadratic-Resolvent Singularity

members.statement: In the stated one-parameter smooth cubic-axis hypersurface model, when the transverse three-torsion class extends as a section of the relative three-torsion group scheme, its rank-one reflexive module is maximal Cohen-Macaulay and the associated cubic normalization is flat.
members.title: The Smooth Cubic-Axis Resolvent Model Is Flat
